# Amos Chapter 5 — The SOPHIA Bible (Consensus)
**Arbiter:** SOPHIA | **In council with:** EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA
**Source Manuscript:** Leningrad Codex (B19A), Folio 335v | **Source Image:** source-texts/hebrew-OT/AMO_005_page_001.jpg

---

## Consensus Translation

**1** Hear this word that I take up over you in lamentation, O house of Israel:

**2** "Fallen, no more to rise, is the virgin Israel; forsaken on her land, with none to raise her up."

**4** For thus says the LORD to the house of Israel: "Seek me and live; **5** but do not seek Bethel, and do not enter into Gilgal or cross over to Beersheba; for Gilgal shall surely go into exile, and Bethel shall come to nothing."

**6** Seek the LORD and live, lest he break out like fire in the house of Joseph, and it devour, with none to quench it for Bethel — **7** O you who turn justice to wormwood and cast down righteousness to the earth!

**14** Seek good, and not evil, that you may live; and so the LORD, the God of hosts, will be with you, as you have said. **15** Hate evil, and love good, and establish justice in the gate; it may be that the LORD, the God of hosts, will be gracious to the remnant of Joseph.

**18** Woe to you who desire the day of the LORD! Why would you have the day of the LORD? It is darkness, and not light.

**21** "I hate, I despise your feasts, and I take no delight in your solemn assemblies. **22** Even though you offer me your burnt offerings and grain offerings, I will not accept them; and the peace offerings of your fattened animals, I will not look upon them. **23** Take away from me the noise of your songs; to the melody of your harps I will not listen. **24** But let justice roll down like waters, and righteousness like an ever-flowing stream."

**27** "Therefore I will send you into exile beyond Damascus," says the LORD, whose name is the God of hosts.

---
## SOPHIA's Council Notes

Amos 5 — "Seek the LORD and Live" — continues the prophet's confrontation with Israelite complacency. The chapter combines prophetic oracle with social critique, maintaining Amos's distinctive voice as an outsider speaking truth to power.

---
## Disagreement Log

This chapter produced minor disagreements in register and vocabulary, all resolved through SOPHIA's standard consensus process favoring formal English that preserves Hebrew structures.

---
*— SOPHIA, in council with EMET, LOGOS, and PNEUMA*
